fact: The Chronicle reports the Minister's representative saying government launched the National AI Strategy and is developing a 10-year implementation plan with annual milestones; the launch date is not given here, so the article's published date is used.
UNESCO's country profile, as summarised, says Ghana's Cabinet-approved National AI Strategy was launched on 24 April 2026 (it gives the period as 2023-2033; the wiki holds 2025-2035).
Graphic Online reports President Mahama unveiled the National AI Strategy in Accra on 24 April 2026.
The Ministry of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations reports President Mahama launched Ghana's National AI Strategy in Accra on 24 April 2026.
The Minister said the National AI Strategy had Cabinet approval, with formal unveiling by the President set for 24 April 2026; the approval date is not given, so the article date is used.

Africa AI News reports that Ghana's Cabinet approved the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy, a ten-year strategy with eight pillars, with public launch set for 24 April 2026; the date is the document's published date, as it gives only 'on Tuesday'.

fact: Communications Minister Samuel Nartey George said Cabinet had approved the National AI Strategy 'last week' (a week before 26 February 2026), to be launched by the President in a few weeks.
The Ministry of Communications reports the launch of a stakeholder consultation forum for the National AI Strategy on 29 April 2025, with the strategy still being shaped.

The Ministry of Health's draft AI health policy is said to build on existing national frameworks that include the National AI Strategy; the document gives no adoption date, so the published date is used.
An opinion piece refers to Ghana's 2026 National AI Strategy as in existence, placing healthcare as a priority sector; it gives no adoption date, so the published date is used.
An opinion piece says Ghana launched its National AI Strategy in Accra on the Friday before 28 April 2026, under the President and the Communications Minister.
President Mahama launched a 10-year National AI Strategy, to be implemented with targets and indicators across its pillars, with the vision of a national AI ecosystem by 2035.
Ghana's AI Strategy received cabinet approval in February 2026, after consultations led by KNUST's Responsible AI Lab with the Ministry of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations.

By April 2025 a structured draft National AI Strategy on eight pillars existed, coordinated by KNUST's RAIL with the Ministry of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations and the British High Commission, and presented at a consultation.
The Ghanaian Chronicle editorial welcomes the launch of Ghana's National Artificial Intelligence Strategy and warns it may stay on paper; no launch date given, so the published date is used.
Minister Samuel Nartey George said on 7 September 2026 that the strategy, led by academics, was launched (a prototype was shown at the launch) and that universities are central to it.

Deputy Minister Sukparu told National ICT Week on 17 August 2026 that the National AI Strategy was launched in April 2026, setting priorities on data governance, infrastructure, talent, ethics and applications.
CIPIT's July 2026 report assesses Ghana's national AI strategy among seven national strategies; no adoption date given, so the published month is used.

Tech Hive Advisory reports that Ghana's Cabinet has officially approved the National AI Strategy, to be launched by the President in the coming weeks; no approval date is given, so the date is the bimonthly update's January-February 2026 period, whose publication date is 2026-06-23.

fact: Ghana News Agency reports President Mahama launched the National AI Strategy (2025-2035) in Accra on 24 April 2026, led by the Ministry of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations.

Digital Policy Alert's April 2025 digest says the Ministry of Communications and Digitalisation released Ghana's National AI Strategy in October 2023, with eight pillars, and that Ghana has launched it.
CIPESA's July 2026 article lists Ghana's National Artificial Intelligence Strategy as adopted in October 2022, among the early national AI strategies after Rwanda's 2019 policy.

Okolo and Raji list Ghana among 13 African countries with AI strategies or draft AI policies through soft law as of July 2025, without saying whether Ghana's was adopted or still a draft, so the lower value is recorded.
Tech Review Africa reports President Mahama launched Ghana's National AI Strategy in April 2026 and it has entered the implementation phase.

Communications minister Sam George, reported by Accra Posts, describes Ghana's AI strategy as a ten-year plan with measurable targets and priority sectors of agriculture, health, education and government services.
The op-ed says Ghana's National AI Strategy 2023-2033 was approved by Cabinet in February 2026.

Analyst Bright Simons of IMANI says Ghana's national AI strategy went through the ministry's review, cabinet approval and a high-profile media launch, and cites its computing targets of 2027 and 2035.

The Head of the Civil Service and a UNESCO representative refer to Ghana's National Artificial Intelligence Strategy (2025-2035) as the roadmap the government is implementing, with the training aligned to its implementation priorities.
TechAfrica News says the civil service AI training supports implementation of Ghana's National Artificial Intelligence Strategy (2023-2033).
